name: cortados-routed-subagents
description: Makes the main session a CortadOS orchestrator: it delegates through the cortados-route MCP tools (start_task / route_task), its own Agent tool calls are refused unless the owner says "fork" in that turn's prompt (then only a fork passes), and a balanced gate (on by default, fails open when the router is unreachable, /cortados-gate off for one session) refuses delegatable work on the main loop, every edit included: the main session plans, delegates, verifies and reports. Subagents spawned below the main loop are routed through the CortadOS provider: S1 picks the cheapest capable model, it runs headless on the provider host, and its tool calls are bridged back to run on this machine. The main session stays on direct Claude.

providerUrl.title: Provider URL
providerUrl.description: CortadOS provider base URL that subagents route through (e.g. the Air on the tailnet).

providerTokenFile.title: Provider token file
providerTokenFile.description: Path to a file holding CORTADOS_PROVIDER_TOKEN. Read fresh at spawn time so the token is never stored in settings. A leading ~ is expanded to $HOME.

providerToken.title: Provider token (inline override)
providerToken.description: Optional inline token. When set it overrides providerTokenFile. Prefer the file so the token is not kept in settings.

model.title: Routed model id
model.description: The model id sent to the provider. 'cortados' lets S1 route; a concrete id pins one lane.

permissionMode.title: Permission mode for routed subagents
permissionMode.description: Headless permission mode. 'bypassPermissions' lets a routed subagent run Bash/edits unattended (full agentic, highest blast radius). 'acceptEdits' auto-approves file edits but blocks unattended Bash. 'default' blocks anything that needs a prompt.

allowedTools.title: Allowed tools (comma-separated)
allowedTools.description: Built-in tools a routed subagent has on this machine, passed as both --tools (availability, the real boundary) and --allowedTools (permission). Tools execute locally (bridged back from the routed model), so this is the real blast-radius control. Built-in tools only; MCP tools are controlled separately.

claudeBin.title: Claude binary
claudeBin.description: The claude executable used to run each routed subagent. Must be on PATH or an absolute path.

routeBackground.title: Route background subagents too
routeBackground.description: On by default (owner decision 2026-11-04: every subagent goes through S1). A background (run_in_background) subagent is started detached under backgroundTimeoutMs, the Agent call answers at once as launched, and the result arrives as a notification from this plugin and in the launch record's outputFile. Off hands background subagents back to native handling.

orchestratorMode.title: Orchestrator mode (brain only plans and delegates)
orchestratorMode.description: When on, a standing directive tells the main session to plan and delegate work through the cortados-route MCP tools (start_task / route_task), the main session's own Agent tool calls are refused (owner rule: an in-process subagent dies with the session's hooks) except a fork the owner asks for by saying "fork" in that turn's prompt, and the orchestrator gate (orchestratorGate, balanced by default) refuses clearly delegatable work on the main loop. Subagents and CortadOS child tasks are unaffected. Off turns all of it off.

orchestratorGate.title: Orchestrator gate level (off, balanced, strict)
orchestratorGate.description: How the main loop is gated in orchestrator mode. 'balanced' (default) refuses clearly delegatable work: WebSearch/WebFetch, NotebookEdit, big edits (over 40 lines or 2000 characters), more than orchestratorEditBudget small edits per user turn (0 by default: every edit), build/test Bash runs and long-running Bash (run_in_background or timeout over 120 s); reading, inspection Bash, Chrome and connector MCP tools stay allowed, and the gate fails open (with a status note) when cortados-route is missing or the provider's /health fails. 'strict' is the allowlist cage (orchestratorAllowedTools). 'off' keeps only the Agent refusal (and its owner-asked fork exception). A mistyped value is 'balanced'. /cortados-gate off|balanced|strict overrides it for one session.

orchestratorEditBudget.title: Small edits per user turn on the main loop (balanced gate)
orchestratorEditBudget.description: Under the balanced gate, how many small Edit/Write/MultiEdit calls the main loop may make itself per user turn before further edits are refused and must be delegated. 0 (the default since 0.3.0) refuses every edit on the main loop; raise it to allow small touches. Big edits are refused at once. A negative or invalid value uses the default.

orchestratorEnforce.title: Orchestrator enforce (alias for orchestratorGate strict)
orchestratorEnforce.description: Backward-compatible alias: true means orchestratorGate 'strict' — every main-loop tool outside orchestratorAllowedTools is refused (the cortados-route tools and the desktop turn plumbing always pass), with no fail-open; it also blocks browser and connector tools. /cortados-gate balanced or off lowers it for one session.

orchestratorAllowedTools.title: Tools the brain MAY use itself on the main loop
orchestratorAllowedTools.description: Used only under the strict gate (orchestratorGate strict or orchestratorEnforce): comma/space-separated allowlist of tools the main loop may run itself. Everything else (edits, shell, web, MCP tools, future tools) is refused and must be delegated. The cortados-route tools (mcp__cortados-route__*) are always allowed, Agent is always refused, and the desktop app's turn plumbing (update_plan, wrap_up, mark_chapter) is never blocked. An empty/invalid value falls back to the default.

subagentTimeoutMs.title: Routed subagent timeout (ms)
subagentTimeoutMs.description: How long a routed foreground subagent may run before it is aborted. Max 600000 (10 min), Claude Code's own limit for a mod's process; larger values are clamped, fractions are rounded down, invalid values use the default. Background subagents use backgroundTimeoutMs.

backgroundTimeoutMs.title: Routed background subagent timeout (ms)
backgroundTimeoutMs.description: How long a routed background subagent may run before its watchdog stops it. Default 7200000 (2 h): real background builders run 30-60+ minutes. Max 10800000 (3 h, the CortadOS child-task limit), because an unattended child that never ends burns quota; larger values are clamped, fractions are rounded down, invalid values use the default. Foreground subagents keep subagentTimeoutMs.

maxTurns.title: Routed subagent max turns
maxTurns.description: Opt-in, off (0) by default. When positive, passed as claude -p --max-turns: a routed subagent stops after this many agentic turns instead of looping until the timeout kills it (incident 2026-11-03). Off by default because there is no evidence yet that a blanket budget is safe for builders, which can legitimately need many turns. A stopped or timed-out subagent still hands back its last assistant text, session id and elapsed time.

excludeBuilderOnReview.title: Keep reviews off the builder's model
excludeBuilderOnReview.description: When on, a review subagent (description matching 'review', or a review subagent type) is sent with x-cortados-exclude-model listing the MAIN SESSION's own model plus the models routed non-review subagents ran on since the last review (up to 3, read from the provider's run record; the list resets on mod reload and after a completed review). If the session model can't be read or the session is itself routed ('cortados'), only the worker models are excluded; if nothing can be excluded, no header is sent and a toast says so.

mainSessionGuard.title: Main-session guard (warn only)
mainSessionGuard.description: When on, a big Edit/Write/NotebookEdit (over 40 lines or 2000 characters of new content) or a build/test Bash run (python -m unittest/pytest, pytest, make, npm/yarn/pnpm build or test) on the MAIN session shows a toast (at most one per 10 minutes) and a status-line counter nudging you to delegate. Never blocks a call. Subagents are never watched. /cortados-guard on|off overrides this, kept in the plugin store.

officeView.title: CortadOS Office view
officeView.description: When on, every routed request carries this session's opaque tag (a salted hash of the session id), the project folder name, the device's short hostname and the task title (the Agent call's description, at most 80 characters), and the main session sends the provider a heartbeat with its status and current tool name, so GET /v1/cortados/office can draw this session as a floor. Metadata only: never prompt text, tool input or file contents.
